title: Replace runtime-exit verbs and evaluator `reason about` vocabulary with static-greppable Python-suppression assertions
summary: The drafter prompt `src/kodezart/prompts/acceptance_criteria.py` emits criteria the in-loop evaluator structurally cannot grade (PR body, CI status, merge state, runtime-exit asks, jointly-unsatisfiable conjunctions), and the evaluator prompt `src/kodezart/prompts/evaluation.py` Watson 3 reads them with a `reason about` verb that re-introduces stochastic falsifiability even when the criteria-gen side is fixed. Rewrite Watson 1 / Watson 3 / Watson 5 asks plus the Sherlock SYNTHESIS section (lines 114-135, EXCLUDING the separate NO-DEFER RULE at lines 137-146 which must be preserved verbatim) in `acceptance_criteria.py`, and mirror the Watson 3 rewrite in `evaluation.py`. EXACTLY TWO files are touched. The standing-rule `.kodezart/` concern from the user scope's third item is intentionally NOT implemented in prompt strings: it is split out to a separate ticket targeting the adapter layer (`GitArtifactPersister`), per the reviewer's [alignment] / [sherlock] guidance and the user's conditional instruction `if no standing-rules list exists, surface the gap rather than invent one`.
context:
## Why this change

Workflow graph in `src/kodezart/chains/ralph_workflow.py` (lines 269-294): `generate_branch -> generate_ticket -> generate_criteria -> (persist_artifacts) -> run_ralph_loop -> merge_to_feature -> review_against_ticket -> open_pr -> monitor_ci -> complete`. The in-loop evaluator inside `run_ralph_loop` runs with `EVAL_TOOLS = ["Read", "Glob", "Grep", "Bash"]` (verified in `src/kodezart/core/constants.py:4`). PR body, CI / check-run status, and merge / branch state are produced strictly AFTER `run_ralph_loop` (`open_pr` at `ralph_workflow.py:870`, `monitor_ci` at `ralph_workflow.py:959`). Any criterion that references those artifacts grades `false` forever inside the loop and the iteration budget burns out regardless of code quality.

Three defect classes, all rooted in prompt strings:

1. Post-loop-artifact criteria. Watson 1 BEHAVIORAL at `acceptance_criteria.py:32-40` says `testable by running a command or inspecting output`; Sherlock SYNTHESIS at `acceptance_criteria.py:128-131` repeats `Testable by running a command or inspecting a file`. Neither bounds `output` / `file` to evidence the in-loop evaluator can collect.

2. Runtime-exit verbs graded by static reasoning. Watson 3 TOOLING at `acceptance_criteria.py:62-73` requests `type checker passes`, `linter reports zero violations`, `all existing and new tests pass`. Evaluator Watson 3 LINT & TYPE SAFETY at `evaluation.py:68-76` reads them with `reason about whether the changes pass both the linter and the type checker` (the literal phrase on lines 71-72). The verb `reason about` lets the Watson read-and-infer, flipping verdicts across iters on identical diffs. Watson 5 INTEGRATION SANITY at `acceptance_criteria.py:100-110` carries the same shape via ask `(b)` at line 106.

3. Joint-unsatisfiability. Five Watsons at `acceptance_criteria.py:31-110` draft independently; Sherlock SYNTHESIS at `acceptance_criteria.py:114-135` cross-references findings but never asks whether the conjunction has any satisfying implementation under the harness's persistence-commit injection. `_persist_artifacts_node` at `ralph_workflow.py:521-557` commits `.kodezart/ticket.json` and `.kodezart/criteria.json` to the ralph branch BEFORE the iter loop begins, so any `exactly N files modified` criterion is structurally unsatisfiable.

The drafter side and evaluator side share one ancestor: the criteria-generation prompts have no model of the evaluator's reach, and the evaluator's vocabulary lets the rewrite be undone at grading time. Both edits must land together or the bug persists.

## Reviewer-feedback responses

(1) [alignment] / [sherlock] split. The previous draft proposed a Mod 3 appending a `.kodezart/`-gitignore standing rule to `_CREATE_PROMPT` in `ticket_generation.py`. That contradicted the user's conditional: `If no such 'always-included standing rules' list exists in the drafter ... surface that gap ... as a finding rather than inventing one. Read before writing.` Investigation (re-verified) confirmed no implementer-facing standing-rules list exists today: `_CREATE_PROMPT` at `ticket_generation.py:6-37` is a drafter-BEHAVIORAL preamble, not a list of rules the drafter embeds into ticket bodies; no other module under `src/kodezart/prompts/` carries such a list either. Mod 3 is REMOVED. The gap is surfaced here. The deterministic `.kodezart/` fix belongs in a separate ticket at the adapter layer — see `out_of_scope` for the recommended shape (`GitArtifactPersister.persist` writes `.kodezart/.gitignore` containing `*` as first action after `mkdir`, OR scopes `.kodezart/` exclusion from `add_all` via explicit pathspec). Note for the follow-up ticket: a self-`.gitignore` does NOT make `GitArtifactPersister.clean()` at `ralph_workflow.py:898-904` redundant — intermediate commits still carry the directory in their tree, and `.gitignore` is not retroactive.

(2) [architecture] correctness vs determinism. The reviewer argued the negative-shape replacements (`no new @ts-ignore`) are strictly weaker than the positive correctness asks (`type checker passes`). The user's explicit scope says `Replace the runtime-exit framing ... with negative-shape static-greppable assertions ... WHY negative-shape: positive runtime claims ('typecheck exits 0') require execution; negative-shape claims ('no new suppression introduced') are falsifiable by grepping the diff.` The user is deliberately trading grading strength for grading determinism — execution-by-Bash is reachable (Bash IS in `EVAL_TOOLS`) but the user judges it stochastic in practice. This ticket honors the user's REPLACE intent and discloses the trade-off explicitly: the in-loop evaluator after this change grades the DIFF SHAPE, not the EXECUTION OUTCOME, of lint/type/test. Engineering-green code that introduces no suppressions on changed lines passes the in-loop gate; the post-merge review and CI are the downstream catches for actual runtime correctness.

(3) [architecture] / [docs] suppression lexicon is Python-only. The previous draft enumerated JS/TS tokens (`@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `as any`, `eslint-disable*`, `.skip`, `.only`, `xdescribe`, `xtest`) verbatim from the user's problem statement, but the user's problem statement used them as EXAMPLES, not as the literal codebase enumeration. kodezart is pure Python (verified: `pyproject.toml:6` `requires-python = ">=3.12"`; no JS/TS source under `src/`). The Python-relevant suppression lexicon is: `# type: ignore` (and bracketed-code form `# type: ignore[<code>]`), `# noqa` (and `# noqa: <code>`), `# ruff: noqa` (and `# ruff: noqa: <code>`), `pytest.mark.skip`, `pytest.mark.skipif`, `pytest.skip(...)` function-call form, `pytest.importorskip(...)`, removed `def test_` declarations on changed lines, removed `assert ` lines on changed lines, and `model_config` whose `extra` value is flipped from `forbid` or `ignore` to `allow` (structural Pydantic config-loosening assertion, not a moral 'schema bypass').

(4) [sanity] SYNTHESIS line range. The previous draft cited `Sherlock SYNTHESIS block at lines 115-146`; verified (re-read) that SYNTHESIS heading is at line 114, body lines 116-135, and NO-DEFER RULE is a SEPARATE block at lines 137-146. The literal `rewrite 115-146` would clobber NO-DEFER RULE. The parallel NO-DEFER RULE block in `_REVIEW_PROMPT_PRELUDE` of `ticket_generation.py` is pinned by `tests/chains/test_ticket_generation.py:336` (verified: `assert "NO-DEFER RULE" in review_prompt`). The corrected range is `rewrite SYNTHESIS body (lines 116-135); preserve NO-DEFER RULE (lines 137-146) verbatim`.

(5) [lint] E501 line-length. Verified: `pyproject.toml:57` sets ruff `line-length = 88`; `pyproject.toml:61` selects rule family `E` which contains E501. The new suppression-token enumeration MUST be formatted multi-line using the file's existing string-content `\<newline>` escape convention (every existing line in `_CRITERIA_PRELUDE` ends with ` \`; this is the documented `\<newline>` escape inside a string literal which resolves to the empty string per docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html#string-literal-concatenation). Each physical source line in the new content must stay at or under 88 characters. Verify with `ruff check src/kodezart/prompts/` after edit.

(6) [docs] documentation citations corrected. The previous draft's claim `backslash line-continuation inside double-quoted strings is standard Python (PEP 8 / language reference, stable since 1.0)` was imprecise. The actual mechanism the existing prompt files use is the string-literal escape sequence `\<newline>` (backslash followed by a newline INSIDE a string literal) which the lexer resolves to the empty string. This is documented at docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html ('Escape sequences'). It is NOT the Python source-code line-continuation primitive (which the same docs page describes as joining LOGICAL lines outside string literals). The new content follows the file's existing in-string escape convention. Equivalent alternative per PEP 8: implicit string concatenation across adjacent string literals (docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html#string-literal-concatenation). The existing files do not use that alternative; new content follows the existing convention.

(7) [sanity] dual-callsite wording for Mod 2. Verified two callsites of `evaluation.build_prompt`: `src/kodezart/chains/ralph_loop.py:206` (in-loop, against ralph branch working tree) and `src/kodezart/chains/ralph_workflow.py:684` (post-merge, against `base..feature_tip` merged diff). The Watson 3 rewrite must NOT say `the ralph branch working tree` exclusively. The correct neutral phrasing is `the changeset under review`. Both callsites pass a `ChangesetDigest` containing file paths and commit subjects (`src/kodezart/types/domain/consolidation.py`); the static-greppable directive works for both because the Watson has the digest plus the diff and can grep both.

(8) [architecture] cross-file canonicalization (SUPPRESSION_TOKENS constant). The reviewer flagged the triple-callsite drift hazard and recommended extracting a typed `SUPPRESSION_TOKENS: tuple[str, ...]` to a new module under `src/kodezart/types/domain/`. This is BLOCKED by the user's edit-set scope (`No file outside src/kodezart/prompts/ is touched`). The current ticket accepts the duplication across `acceptance_criteria.py` Watson 3 and `evaluation.py` Watson 3 as a deliberate scope-bounded compromise. The drift hazard is documented in `openQuestions`. A follow-up ticket should extract the constant when the constraints surface allows touching `src/kodezart/types/domain/`.

(9) [sanity] iteration_feedback.py awareness. Re-read confirms `src/kodezart/prompts/iteration_feedback.py:42-51` contains its own `WATSON 5: ANTI-PATTERN GUARD` block including the literal `"graceful degradation"` at line 45 — pinned indirectly by `tests/prompts/test_prompt_wiring.py:45` (verified: `assert "graceful degradation" in output`). However, `iteration_feedback.py` is the FIXER prompt for ralph-loop iter 2+: it does NOT draft acceptance criteria, and it does NOT grade them. It is OFF the bifurcation path between criteria-gen and evaluation. Touching it would broaden the change beyond the defect this ticket closes. Documented in `out_of_scope`; a follow-up ticket should consolidate the anti-pattern guidance when a constants module is introduced.

(10) [sherlock] mutual-satisfiability self-check is in-prompt best-effort. The reviewer correctly notes that pushing feasibility logic onto the LLM with no code-level audit is functionally a self-graded pass. Implementing it as a typed `ConditionalEdge` graph node is BLOCKED by the user's constraint (`no new graph node, no new round-trip, no schema change`). The wording in Sherlock SYNTHESIS step (iii) must therefore acknowledge `this is a best-effort feasibility check, not a hard guard; if the LLM emits an unsatisfiable conjunction it will surface as an iteration failure downstream`. Disclosed in-prompt so future readers understand the limitation.

## Verified test surface

- `tests/prompts/test_prompt_wiring.py:20-47` pins `WATSON 1` and `graceful degradation` and the task-description / criteria input strings. `graceful degradation` lives in Watson 4 ANTI-PATTERN of `acceptance_criteria.py:79` and Watson 2 ARCHITECTURE of `evaluation.py:54` and Watson 5 ANTI-PATTERN GUARD of `iteration_feedback.py:45`. None of these three sites are touched by this change. All three pinned strings survive.
- `tests/chains/test_ticket_generation.py:332-336` pins `You are Sherlock`, `WATSON 1: ALIGNMENT`, `WATSON 4: OFFICIAL DOCS`, `Medium articles`, `NO-DEFER RULE` inside `_REVIEW_PROMPT_PRELUDE` of `ticket_generation.py`. This changedoes NOT touch `ticket_generation.py` (Mod 3 dropped). The pinned strings survive.
- No tests pin `_CREATE_PROMPT` or the SYNTHESIS body of `acceptance_criteria.py` or the Watson 3 body of `evaluation.py` (verified by grep across `tests/`). The proposed edits land green against the existing test suite.

## Documentation sources consulted (corrected)

This change is purely prompt-string editing inside Python module-level constants. No library API surface is modified. Verified:
- `pyproject.toml:55-65` ruff `lint.select = ["E","W","F","I","B","C4","UP","N","ANN","S","A","ARG","RUF"]` with `line-length = 88`. Rule E501 (line-too-long) WILL fire on any physical source line in `_CRITERIA_PRELUDE` or `_EVALUATION_PRELUDE` that exceeds 88 chars. The suppression-token enumeration in the proposed edits MUST be split across multiple physical lines using the file's existing `\<newline>` in-string escape convention.
- `pyproject.toml:39-44` mypy `strict = true`, `disallow_any_explicit = true`. String-content edits do not change type signatures.
- Python lexical-analysis reference (docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html, section 'String and Bytes literals') documents the `\<newline>` escape inside string literals as resolving to the empty string. The existing prompt files use this convention; the new content follows it.
- Pydantic v2 model config (docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/models/, section 'Model Config / Extra fields') documents `extra: 'allow' | 'forbid' | 'ignore'`. `extra='allow'` is a legitimate option, not a 'bypass'. The criterion shape is therefore structural: `no Pydantic model config flips its 'extra' value from 'forbid' or 'ignore' to 'allow' on changed lines`.
- LangGraph (`langgraph>=0.2.0`): graph topology in `ralph_workflow.py` is untouched. No LangGraph API call is added or removed.
- claude-agent-sdk (`claude-agent-sdk~=0.1.69`): prompt strings are passed verbatim to `service.stream(prompt=...)` at `ralph_workflow.py:411-424` and `689-703` and `ralph_loop.py:206`. No SDK surface is touched.

Preserve every line of the file outside the four blocks named below; in particular preserve the NO-DEFER RULE block at lines 137-146 VERBATIM (it is a SEPARATE block from SYNTHESIS and the parallel block in `ticket_generation.py::_REVIEW_PROMPT_PRELUDE` is pinned by `tests/chains/test_ticket_generation.py:336`).
